Sarah Huckabee Sanders

Republican candidate for Governor, Arkansas · Incumbent

Governor of Arkansas (incumbent)

Sarah Huckabee Sanders is the Republican governor of Arkansas and took office on January 10, 2023. She is seeking a second term in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Fred Love and Libertarian Colt Shelby. Before becoming governor, she was White House press secretary under President Donald Trump from 2017 to 2019.

Where Sanders stands

Taxes
Supports continuing to cut the state income tax. She said the goal is to reach zero and planned a special session after the 2026 fiscal session to lower the personal income tax rate by another 0.2 percentage points.
Taxes
Supports cutting the corporate income tax rate. She says holding the line on new spending would let the state cut taxes and stay in good financial shape.
Education
Supports the LEARNS Act, which she signed. It created Education Freedom Accounts, publicly funded accounts that pay for private school and homeschool costs. She defended the program during the October 2026 debate.
Prisons and public safety
Her FY2026-27 budget request did not include new money for the proposed Franklin County prison. She said she is open to prison reform ideas.
Regulation and economic development
Issued Executive Order 26-04 in February 2026 directing state agencies to review permits, licenses, and approvals. In October 2026 she announced 344 regulatory changes meant to speed up permitting.

Background

  • Governor of Arkansas, 2023–present (47th governor)
  • White House Press Secretary, 2017–2019
  • White House Deputy Press Secretary, 2017
  • Elected governor in 2022 with 63.0% of the general election vote
  • Born August 13, 1982, in Little Rock, Arkansas
